Quantile Function for the Product of Three Normal Variables

Source: R/qprodnormal3.R
qprodnormal3.Rd

Computes the quantile q with P(X1 * X2 * X3 <= q) = p (or > q, for lower.tail = FALSE) where (X1, X2, X3) follows a trivariate normal distribution with mean vector mean and covariance matrix cov. It inverts pprodnormal3() by root-finding, bracketed by the delta-method interval, and is the same routine behind dist_quantile() for a ProductNormal3 object.

Usage

qprodnormal3(p, mean, cov, lower.tail = TRUE, tol = 1e-06)

Arguments

p

Numeric vector of probabilities in [0, 1], no missing values. 0 and 1 return -Inf and Inf (reversed for lower.tail = FALSE).

mean

Numeric vector of means of length 3.

cov

3x3 covariance matrix, as for pprodnormal3().

lower.tail

Logical; if TRUE (default) p is P(X1 * X2 * X3 <= q), otherwise P(X1 * X2 * X3 > q). The upper tail is inverted through the directly integrated upper tail of pprodnormal3(), so a small upper-tail p is resolved.

tol

Positive tolerance used for both the CDF evaluation and the root-finder (default 1e-6). It is absolute, so for a probability p use a tol well below p; pprodnormal3() explains why.

Value

A numeric vector the same length and names as p. Three zero-variance components give a point mass, whose quantile is prod(mean) for any p strictly between 0 and 1.

See also

pprodnormal3() for the CDF, qprodnormal() for two factors, dist_quantile() for the object interface.

Examples

qprodnormal3(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), mean = c(1, 1, 1), cov = diag(3))
#> [1] -2.7142556  0.2704444  8.0329270
# an upper-tail probability of 1e-8, resolved with a matching tolerance
qprodnormal3(1e-8, mean = c(1, 1, 1), cov = diag(3), lower.tail = FALSE, tol = 1e-12)
#> [1] 73.10362
